messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1769564321 - us-west-2c: Elevated ELB 5xx and EBS IO latency observed. Initial detection by synthetic checks.

jamie (oncall): grabbing this. seeing ELB 5xx spike ~18:02 UTC and app timeouts for a subset of instances in us-west-2c. paging SRE.

miguel (sre): joining. prelim: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn $TG` -> intermittent Unhealthy. CloudWatch shows EBSIOQueueDepth high and ENI drops increasing. Running deeper host checks.

ryan (eng-runtime): logs show many `connection reset by peer` around the same window. Runtime telemetry: token emission fine, but transport errors up. Could be NIC or hypervisor.

elaine (support): customer impact: 9 high-touch customers reporting 503s/timeouts (finapp-alpha, media-ingest, searchsvc-prod). ETA to publish initial status?

jamie (oncall): publish now, include mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic off us-west-2c via Route53 latency policy and weight adjustment, 2) start draining targets in us-west-2c, 3) migrate affected EBS-backed instances if host-level IO persists.

status-bot: INCIDENT CREATED 1769564350 - Severity: partial outage (region AZ-specific).

miguel (sre): running host-level probe: `ssh host123` -> dmesg shows repeated network driver resets and EBS detach/re-attach logs. Opening console ticket with cloud provider ops.

ryan (eng-runtime): pushing a temporary smart-router override to prefer us-west-2a/b for new sessions. Command in router: `POST /config {"az_preference":["us-west-2a","us-west-2b"]}`. This should avoid establishing new connections into impacted AZ.

miguel (sre): initiating ELB target drain for us-west-2c. `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn $TG --targets Id=...` with deregistration delay set to 240s. Also increasing healthcheck frequency in our internal probe to speed up failover detection.

elaine (support): drafted status: "Partial degradation in us-west-2c causing elevated 5xx and timeouts for some customers. Traffic is being shifted and we are investigating underlying host/network issues." Post? :pencil2:

jamie (oncall): post it. add note for customers with dedicated nodes—may need manual migration.

status-bot: STATUS PAGE UPDATE POSTED 1769564400 - https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1769564321

miguel (sre): cloud provider acknowledged potential hypervisor NIC firmware regression. They recommend instance live-migrate. Starting live-migrate for 8 affected instances. Tracking: MIGRATE-1769.

ryan (eng-runtime): after routing override, p95 latency for API down from 2.1s -> 520ms, 5xx rate for the region down from 9.4% -> 1.1% (aggregated). Good early signal.

ali (prod-sre): confirm capacity in us-west-2a/b to take extra load. We should also warm caches in those AZs to avoid cold-start latencies.

ryan (eng-runtime): priming hot keys and pre-populating KV caches now. Results: cache hit rate rising, tail latencies smoothing out.

miguel (sre): live-migrate step 1/8 complete. Observed EBS io wait drop on migrated instance from 120ms -> 18ms. Host-level ENI drop counters also decreased post-migration.

elaine (support): customer update #2 sent to impacted customers with recommended retry/backoff and note we shifted traffic. Responses: mixed; a couple asked for SOC-level notification.

jamie (oncall): action items: miguel continue migration & host isolation, ryan keep router override until metrics stable for 15m, elaine coordinate customer comms and support escalations, ali prepare postmortem checklist. I'm handing primary to miguel at 1769566200 (20:30 UTC).

miguel (sre): taking over. filing internal follow-up: reduce Route53 healthcheck interval and lower TTL for critical records to improve automated failover in the future. Observed that Route53 health probes from one vantage spiked ~30s lag delaying automatic failover.

status-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 1769565600 - Mitigation in progress. Impact: Partial (subset of customers). Next update ETA: 1769567400.

ryan (eng-runtime): note: one of our NLBs showed stale connection tracking entries causing some connections to be reset during the AZ shift. We're rotating NLBs in the control plane to clear state.

miguel (sre): migration 5/8 complete. Two instances required full stop/start to re-attach volumes cleanly; those customers on dedicated hardware may see longer windows.

elaine (support): support queue update: 24 tickets, triage priority P1 for 3 accounts, others P2. Customer comms drafted for dedicated customers with manual migration steps.

ali (prod-sre): prepare rollback plan: if shifting causes increased latency in other AZs, revert router override and scale up capacity, monitor error budgets closely.

jamie (oncall): good. I'm adding runbook link and handoff notes to the thread before I go.

miguel (sre): final migration complete 8/8 at 1769567100. Metrics: EBSIOWait normalized in us-west-2c hosts that were migrated; ELB 5xx in the AZ down to 0.8%. Holding weighted/latency routing for 10 more minutes for stability.

status-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED 1769567200 - Recovery trending. Postmortem scheduled.

elaine (support): posted final customer update: "We completed host migration and traffic stabilization. Some customers using dedicated nodes in us-west-2c may require follow-up. A postmortem will follow."

jamie (oncall): handing off final ownership to prod-sre for postmortem. I'm offline now. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

miguel (sre): filing RCA ticket: suspected hypervisor NIC firmware + EBS path congestion -> host-level network driver resets -> target Unhealthy -> ELB 5xx. Follow-ups: firmware rollout check, Route53 healthcheck config, NLB connection-tracking hardening, dedicated-customer migration playbook.

status-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED 1769568000 - Partial outage mitigated; postmortem to be published.
